outcomes.reason: ["Clause 3 (delegation to the Administrator for Industrial Recovery to determine whether an organization is a bona fide cooperative) has no fixed first end. Three held orders bear on it and the shared analysis reaches none of them: (a) the order of September 27, 1934 creating the National Industrial Recovery Board (EO 6859) authorized the Board 'to exercise all those powers heretofore conferred by Executive orders upon the Administrator for Industrial Recovery', which moves the exercise of the function to the Board without expressly revoking the delegation, and the held text does not show whether it displaced the Administrator's delegation (a transfer of exercise is not shown to be an end); (b) the order of June 15, 1935 reorganizing the NRA (EO 7075) terminated the Board and let a new Administrator of the National Recovery Administration exercise 'all of those powers heretofore conferred by Executive Order upon the National Industrial Recovery Board'; (c) the order of June 15, 1935 extending the NRA's activities (EO 7076) amended all existing Title I orders 'so as to continue them in effect' to April 1, 1936 'so far as consistent' with Title I as amended, with a proviso that it authorizes no approval or enforcement of codes. EO 7075 and EO 7076 are orders issued on or after June 14, 1935 and organizational orders, which the shared analysis lists as outside its scope. Whether the determination power ended with the June 14, 1935 repeal (because the 'benefits and protection of this order' it serves, the code constructions in clauses 1 and 2, ended then), or continued until April 1, 1936 or the January 1, 1936 termination of the NRA (EO 7252), turns on whether it is code-dependent, a question the analysis does not decide, and no held record shows any determination ever made under it. Needed: a source or legal analysis fixing the effect of EO 6859, EO 7075 and EO 7076 on delegations to the Administrator, or an owner ruling that a determination power ancillary to code constructions ends with the code-enforcement repeal.", "Clause 1 extends beyond codes to any 'agreement or license' approved, prescribed or issued under title I (while framing the rule as to a 'violation of any code of fair competition'). The shared analysis excludes section 4(a) agreements (authority that continued to April 1, 1936 under section 1 of S.J. Res. 113) and section 4(b) licenses (authority that expired June 16, 1934). Whether clause 1 reached agreements or licenses independently of any code, and so outlived June 14, 1935 or ended June 16, 1934 for licenses, is not settled by the held text.", "The order supplements EO 6355. No held record ends EO 6355 and its lifecycle is unclaimed, so any end of the parent that would carry the supplement with it is not established; the later general order of August 21, 1934 delegating functions to the Federal Alcohol Control Administration (EO 6829) lists EO 6606-A among the orders that still apply to alcohol codes, which shows continued application on that date and is not an end. The dossier's machine lead 'target provision not located: EO 6829' is that recital, not an end."]
